authors: Ministry of Home Affairs (Govt. of India)
venue: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 432, 2 Dec 2025
title: Cases of cybercrime: NCRP complaints, citizen losses and CFCFRMS savings, 2022-2024
problem_addressed: Scale of cyber fraud and performance of the national reporting and freeze system
main_finding: Losses rose from Rs 2,290.24 cr (2022) to Rs 22,845.73 cr (2024); 22.68 lakh NCRP incidents in 2024; CFCFRMS saved over Rs 7,130 cr across 23.02 lakh complaints
stated_or_observed_limitation: Aggregate figures only; no victim-level timing or journey data

title: Bank frauds and digital payment frauds in India, FY2024-25
problem_addressed: Volume and value of frauds reported by banks
main_finding: Digital payment frauds were 13,516 cases, 56.5% of all reported bank fraud cases, worth about Rs 520 cr
stated_or_observed_limitation: Bank-reported frauds only; excludes unreported victimisation

title: 1 in 5 families surveyed have someone using UPI confirm experiencing UPI fraud once or more in the last 3 years
problem_addressed: Household experience of UPI fraud and reporting behaviour
main_finding: About 1 in 5 UPI families had experienced fraud in three years; about half of victims did not report it
stated_or_observed_limitation: Self-selected online sample; self-reported experience

authors: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
venue: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in), accessed Nov 2026
title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline: complaint and financial-fraud reporting workflow
problem_addressed: How a victim is meant to report financial cyber fraud
dataset_or_testbed: Portal workflow, 1930 helpline and CFCFRMS routing
main_finding: A 1930 call or portal complaint creates a ticket that is routed to banks through CFCFRMS so funds can be put on hold
stated_or_observed_limitation: Documentation states the intended workflow, not how victims experience it

authors: C. Cross, R. G. Smith and K. Richards
venue: Trends & Issues in Crime and Criminal Justice, no. 544, Australian Institute of Criminology
title: The reporting experiences and support needs of victims of online fraud
problem_addressed: What victims experience when they report online fraud and what support they need
method: Survey and interviews with fraud victims
main_finding: Victims met blame, disbelief and poor communication when reporting, and many did not report at all
stated_or_observed_limitation: Australian setting; romance and investment frauds dominate

authors: M. T. Whitty and T. Buchanan
venue: Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking, vol. 15, no. 3
title: The online romance scam: A serious cybercrime
problem_addressed: Psychological impact of online fraud on victims
main_finding: Victims reported severe emotional impact, shame and self-blame, which suppressed disclosure
stated_or_observed_limitation: Romance scams only; financial recovery not studied

venue: Communications of the ACM, vol. 54, no. 3
title: Understanding scam victims: Seven principles for systems security
problem_addressed: Why intelligent people comply with scams
main_finding: Time pressure and social compliance are two of seven principles that switch off careful reasoning
stated_or_observed_limitation: Principles derived from cases, not experimentally tested

title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
problem_addressed: General principles of compliance
method: Synthesis of experimental and field research
main_finding: Authority, liking and scarcity reliably raise compliance, including under time pressure
stated_or_observed_limitation: General persuasion, not fraud recovery

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
problem_addressed: How fast and slow thinking shape judgement
main_finding: Under load and time pressure, fast intuitive System 1 dominates and stored knowledge is not retrieved
stated_or_observed_limitation: Framework, not fraud-specific evidence

title: Decision making under stress: A selective review
problem_addressed: How acute stress changes decision making
main_finding: Acute stress shifts decisions toward habit and away from goal-directed, deliberative choice
stated_or_observed_limitation: Laboratory stressors differ from real financial loss

authors: D. Modic, R. Anderson and J. Palomaki
title: We will make you like our research: The development of a susceptibility-to-persuasion scale (StP-II)
problem_addressed: Individual differences in scam susceptibility
main_finding: Traits including premeditation, self-control and susceptibility to authority predict compliance
stated_or_observed_limitation: Self-report traits; behaviour not observed in real frauds

authors: R. M. Titus and A. R. Gover
title: Personal fraud: The victims and the scams
problem_addressed: Who fraud victims are and how they respond
main_finding: Many victims delayed or avoided reporting and blamed themselves; losses were often discovered late
stated_or_observed_limitation: Pre-smartphone, pre-UPI setting

authors: H. S. Jones, J. N. Towse, N. Race and T. Harrison
title: Email fraud: The search for psychological predictors of susceptibility
problem_addressed: Whether speed of response predicts phishing susceptibility
main_finding: Participants who responded quickly were worse at telling phishing from genuine mail
stated_or_observed_limitation: Email, not voice or payment fraud; student-heavy sample

authors: E. J. Williams, J. Hinds and A. N. Joinson
venue: International Journal of Human-Computer Studies, vol. 120
title: Exploring susceptibility to phishing in the workplace
problem_addressed: How authority and urgency cues affect workplace phishing
main_finding: Authority cues in messages increased link clicks at scale
stated_or_observed_limitation: Workplace email context; recovery behaviour not measured

authors: M. De Bona and F. Paci
venue: Proc. 15th Int. Conf. Availability, Reliability and Security (ARES)
title: A real world study on employees' susceptibility to phishing attacks
problem_addressed: Which persuasion cues work in real phishing
main_finding: Urgency was more effective than authority in producing compliance
stated_or_observed_limitation: Single organisation; email channel only

authors: K. T. Mai, S. Bray, T. Davies and L. D. Griffin
title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes
problem_addressed: Whether people can hear that a voice is cloned
main_finding: Listeners identified deepfake speech only 73% of the time; training examples helped only slightly
stated_or_observed_limitation: Detection task, not a live scam call

title: Beware the Artificial Impostor: A McAfee cybersecurity artificial intelligence report
problem_addressed: Prevalence of AI voice scams
dataset_or_testbed: 7,054 adults in seven countries, incl. 1,010 in India
main_finding: 47% of Indian respondents had experienced, or knew someone who had experienced, an AI voice scam, close to double the global average
stated_or_observed_limitation: Vendor survey; self-reported exposure

venue: Which? / Deltapoll victim survey, reported Oct 2026
title: Reporting a scam: where victims tell, and where the process fails them
problem_addressed: Where fraud victims report and what goes wrong when they do
dataset_or_testbed: 1,501 UK adults who lost money to fraud in the past two years
main_finding: Three quarters told their bank but only about 1 in 6 told police; about 3 in 5 hit a problem when reporting, including queues and being passed between departments
stated_or_observed_limitation: UK setting and institutions

title: UPI product statistics, FY2024-25
problem_addressed: Scale of the payment rail on which most retail fraud occurs
main_finding: UPI processed 185.8 billion transactions in FY2024-25, 83.4% of India's digital payment volume
stated_or_observed_limitation: Volume statistics only; no fraud-journey data

title: Illicit financial flows from cyber-enabled fraud
problem_addressed: How cyber-fraud proceeds move and are laundered
main_finding: Fraud proceeds are layered through mule accounts and converted within hours, so interception must be near-real-time
stated_or_observed_limitation: Global scope; limited victim-side detail

title: Internet Organised Crime Threat Assessment (IOCTA) 2024
problem_addressed: Organised cyber-enabled fraud operations
main_finding: Fraud is run as an organised, cross-border service industry with rapid cash-out
stated_or_observed_limitation: European enforcement perspective

venue: Workshop on the Economics of Information Security (WEIS)
title: Measuring the changing cost of cybercrime
problem_addressed: Where the costs of cybercrime fall
main_finding: Indirect and defence costs, including victim time and distress, exceed direct losses for many frauds
stated_or_observed_limitation: Cost accounting, not journey timing

authors: T. Moore, R. Clayton and R. Anderson
venue: Journal of Economic Perspectives, vol. 23, no. 3
title: The economics of online crime
problem_addressed: Why online crime persists despite technical defences
main_finding: Misaligned incentives between banks, platforms and police leave victims carrying the cost of coordination
stated_or_observed_limitation: Pre-dates India's current reporting system

title: Combating mule fraud: Adopting a tech-enabled human-led approach
problem_addressed: Mule accounts in Indian cyber fraud and how to disrupt them
method: Industry analysis of I4C and RBI data
main_finding: I4C flagged over 24 lakh mule-linked accounts/SIMs ecosystem-wide; disruption needs bank, telecom and police action together
stated_or_observed_limitation: Industry report; methods not peer reviewed

authors: M. Gupta and R. K. Singh
venue: Indian Journal of Legal Review, vol. 5, no. 5
title: Cyber crime and investigation in India: Role of law enforcement and challenges faced
problem_addressed: Capacity and coordination of Indian cybercrime investigation
dataset_or_testbed: Indian laws, agencies and case material
main_finding: Jurisdictional problems, limited training, weak coordination and low digital awareness constrain investigation
stated_or_observed_limitation: Doctrinal method; no primary victim data

title: Crime in India 2022
problem_addressed: Recorded cybercrime volumes and disposal
main_finding: Recorded cybercrime greatly exceeds charge-sheeting and conviction, showing a wide gap between reporting and resolution
stated_or_observed_limitation: Recorded crime only; reporting portal complaints are counted separately

venue: Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) research paper, May 2026
title: The impact of fraud on financial inclusion in the UK
problem_addressed: How fraud and institutional responses affect victims' financial inclusion
dataset_or_testbed: Over 2,000 low- and middle-income UK households
main_finding: Around 30% of low-income and 40% of middle-income victims received no reimbursement; about 80% reported a decline in financial inclusion after fraud
stated_or_observed_limitation: UK reimbursement regime differs from India's

title: Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
problem_addressed: Who bears the loss from an unauthorised transaction
dataset_or_testbed: All scheduled banks and prepaid instrument issuers
main_finding: Zero customer liability for third-party breaches reported within 3 working days; capped liability at 4-7 days; banks must shadow-credit within 10 working days and resolve within 90 days
stated_or_observed_limitation: Covers unauthorised transactions; authorised (tricked) payments largely fall outside it

title: Annual Fraud Report 2024
problem_addressed: Scale and reimbursement of UK payment fraud
main_finding: Authorised push payment fraud is a major loss category and most cases begin on online platforms
stated_or_observed_limitation: UK data and definitions

venue: PSR policy statement and rules, in force 7 Oct 2024
title: Requiring reimbursement for authorised push payment (APP) scams
problem_addressed: Whether victims who were tricked into paying should be reimbursed
main_finding: Sending and receiving payment firms must share the cost of reimbursing APP victims up to GBP 85,000, with a decision expected within five business days in most cases
stated_or_observed_limitation: UK regime; India has no equivalent rule for authorised payments

venue: Workshop on the Economics of Information Security (WEIS)
title: Why do Nigerian scammers say they are from Nigeria?
problem_addressed: Economics of scammer targeting
main_finding: Scammers optimise for the most compliant victims, so the victims who reach the payment stage are the least likely to self-protect quickly
stated_or_observed_limitation: Modelling study of one fraud type

authors: Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services (Govt. of India)
venue: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2481, answered 15 Dec 2025
title: Rise in cybercrimes and fraud linked to UPI
problem_addressed: Trend in UPI and digital payment fraud
dataset_or_testbed: RBI and NPCI data, FY2021-22 to FY2025-26
main_finding: UPI fraud was 12.64 lakh incidents worth Rs 981 cr in FY2024-25, down slightly from 13.42 lakh and Rs 1,087 cr in FY2023-24
stated_or_observed_limitation: Channel statistics only; no reporting-delay data
